title: Capacity pool sprint-credit simulator and pricing sketch
body:
Purpose:
This working sheet tests a new pricing / allocation mechanism for Dedicated GPU pools that we call "sprint credits": fixed monthly credit allocations that teams draw down in high-throughput windows (sprints) and that can be inflated/deflated by an elasticity score to smooth utilization across the pool. The goal is to improve steady-state utilization while preserving predictable revenue and an easy buyer mental model.

High-level idea (short):
- Customers buy monthly sprint-credit bundles (e.g., 1000, 5000, 20k credits). Each credit ~= 1 GPU-hour at baseline 16GB V100-equivalent pricing.
- During any hour, a tenant consumes credits at a rate adjusted by their workload elasticity score. Low-latency critical workloads have lower elasticity (consume more credits per GPU-hour); best-effort batch jobs get a backfill multiplier discount.
- Unused credits roll forward up to a cap. Surplus pool capacity is offered to backfill at deep-discount ephemeral rates; discounts are accounted for as negative amortization in the pool P&L.

Inputs (sheet sections):
- Pool configuration: pool_id, region, gpu_type, total_gpus, avg_gpu_hour_cost ($), fixed_monthly_opex ($), target_utilization (%), SLA_weight (0-1)
- Customer slices: tenant_id, bought_credits_monthly, baseline_credit_rate (credit per gpu-hour), elasticity_score (0.1-2.0), expected_sprint_hours/month, preferred_sla_class (gold/silver/batch)
- Backfill policy: backfill_discount (percent), max_backfill_share_of_pool (%), preemption_penalty ($/evicted-job), rollforward_cap_days

Key computed columns (examples):
- effective_credit_consumption = baseline_credit_rate * elasticity_score * actual_gpu_hours_used
- revenue_per_month = sum(bought_credits * list_price_per_credit) + ephemeral_backfill_revenue
- realized_gpu_hours = sum(actual_gpu_hours_used by tenant) + backfill_gpu_hours
- pool_utilization = realized_gpu_hours / (total_gpus * hours_in_month)
- marginal_cost_per_credit = (avg_gpu_hour_cost * total_hours + fixed_monthly_opex) / expected_credits_sold
- amortized_gpu_cost_per_tenant = (tenant_effective_hours / realized_gpu_hours) * total_pool_cost

Sample table (first 6 rows):
Pool: west-1-gp1, total_gpus=120, avg_gpu_hour_cost=1.95, fixed_opex=28,000, target_util=0.78
Tenants:
- tenant A: bought_credits=5,000, baseline_rate=1.0, elasticity=0.9, expected_sprint_h=40
- tenant B: bought_credits=20,000, baseline_rate=1.0, elasticity=1.6, expected_sprint_h=200
- tenant C (batch): bought_credits=10,000, baseline_rate=1.0, elasticity=0.45, expected_sprint_h=600 (eligible for backfill)
Calculated outputs (example):
- expected_realized_hours (base) = 8400h, backfill_capacity_hours = 1200h, pool_utilization ~= 0.82
- list_price_per_credit = $1.40 (suggested), marginal_cost_per_credit ~= $0.92, gross_margin ~34%

Sensitivity experiments included in the sheet tabs (controls at top):
1) Elasticity distribution shift: simulate what happens to utilization and margin if more tenants have low elasticity (more batch).
2) Sprint clustering: simulate 1-week concentrated sprints vs even spread, measure queueing/backfill and SLA breach risk.
3) Rollforward cap toggle: 0/30/90 days and customer churn impact on revenue recognition.
4) Backfill depth: change backfill_discount from 40% to 85% and observe effective marginal cost and realized margin.

Preliminary recommendations (for discussion):
- Introduce a 3-tier sprint-credit list price with clear per-credit equivalent in GPU-hours (small/medium/large bundles) to keep packaging simple for buyers.
- Default elasticity profiles by SLA class (gold=1.0, silver=1.3, batch=0.5) but allow customers to request manual elasticity adjustments with a runtime penalty SLA.
- Keep backfill cap <= 15% of pool to avoid revenue cannibalization; use aggressive preemption signals so critical tenants are unaffected.
- Offer an annual commitment option that converts unspent monthly credits into reduced list price to improve commitability.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Need to run historical telemetry mapping: correlate per-tenant request/seq-length distributions to derive an observed elasticity proxy (RDW-4821).
- Validate customer willingness to buy "credits" vs. pure capacity commits — run 3 sales pilots with current Dedicated customers.
- Build a calculator UI for Console that maps credits <-> estimated SLOs and shows worst-case preemption exposure.
- Product/legal: how to present rollforward and refund policy in contract terms.

Appendix (notes on modelling choices):
- We intentionally priced credits near but below the simple GPU-hour equivalence to make the rollforward/backfill economics visible.
- Elasticity is a blending parameter (workload sensitivity to latency/throughput). We model it as multiplicative on credit draw rate; other models (additive, bucketed) are possible and the sheet contains both to compare.
- All per-hour cost numbers currently use spot-weighted blended historical pricing from accounting; replace with region-specific cloud quotes in later iterations.

Quick links & refs:
- Spreadsheet tabs: overview | inputs | per-tenant-sim | sensitivity | p&l | sales-pricing-sheet
- Relevant tickets: RDW-4310 (console-pricing-exposure), RDW-4821 (usage-telemetry), GH infra#842 (allocator changes)

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally a working prototype — numbers are illustrative. Focus review on the sensitivity outcomes and whether the sprint-credit package simplifies sales conversations without introducing unacceptable revenue volatility.
- If we like the model, next step: convert the core sims into a lightweight service used by the quoting flow and include a backfill simulation on the resource manager side.
